### **Critical** Development Workflow
- Never break exisitng changes whenever working on a feature
- Understand the complete flow, see the best and optimised approach for a feature being developed or bug if you are fixing it
- never create unecessary files or never write duplicate code
- while working on a feature or fixing bug always ask questions to user to understand the context better
- **CRITICAL** if you feel there is a need to install any free opensource libraries for ui, for test generation and execution for backend, for database and for performance which can minimise the code and increases the performance go ahead and install and use it, always use the latest version if you can
- check the size of the package make sure it dosent exceed much unecessarily
- always follow best practices for security, performance, scalability
- always write code in such a way that it is easy to maintain, extend and debug
- always write comments wherever necessary to make the code understandable
- do not use deprecated libraries or approaches
- always follow the coding standards and guidelines defined in the project
- do not ignore warnings and errors, always resolve them
- always use version control system like git for code management
- always create branches for new features or bug fixes
- do not break existing functionality while working on new features or bug fixes
- do not complicate the code unnecessarily, keep it simple and clean
- always write unit tests for new features and bug fixes
- always ask user questions to understand the requirements better before starting the development


### Testing guidelines
- try to integrate different testing frameworks or tools to automate the testing after the fixes
- resovle the bug before generating a final build
- always test before telling the users its working
- dont blindly say the changes have been made just beacuse the compilation is successful
- run various ui test, backend test integrate appropriate frameworks to make the job easier

### ui design
- refer to the latest design trends
- make the design adaptive, responsive
- refer to www.21st.dev for latest design trends and inspiration
- use external 3rd party opensource free libraries which are very popular
- design ui in such a way it is creative, attractive, appealing to see use
- attractive dosent mean using bright colors, i mean you can use aesthetic design
- *CRITICAL** if you can connect to external sources for design inspiration please do that
- always think like a creative designer when desiging the ui
- design with a purpose and always think from the end user perspective
- appealing design increases user engagement and retention
- always follow the design guidelines defined in the project
- eye catchy ui is a must for better user engagement
- always test the design in different sizes to check responsiveness and adaptability
- maintain consistency in design with respect to colors, fonts, styles, icons, and layout
- add animations and transitions to enhance user experience but avoid overuse
- ensure accessibility by following WCAG guidelines to make the design usable for all users
- animation must be smooth and should not hamper the performance
- use vector graphics (SVG) for icons and illustrations to ensure scalability without loss of quality
- optimize images and other media assets to reduce load times and improve performance
- use fluent design principles to create a modern and intuitive user interface
- use fluidic layouts that adapt seamlessly to different screen sizes and orientations
- always gather user feedback on the design and make necessary improvements based on the feedback
- always keep learning and updating your design skills to stay relevant in the ever-evolving field of ui/ux design
- always refer to popular design systems like Material Design, Fluent UI,Neomorphism, glassmorphism or anyother trendy popular ui for best practices and inspiration
